pages.narrative: These panels were created for the 360 Condominiums in Austin, TX. Panels are a great way to cover the walls without the cost of on site painting. Also, they can be removed after relocation and be used elsewhere.

pages.title: Andy Roddick Mural
pages.narrative: This mural was painted for tennis champion, Andy Roddick. Andy wanted an inspirational mural for his home gym. Andy's interior decorator, Sandy Senter, called us, and after consultation and a design stage, this was the mural decided upon. The mural includes Andy's personal heroes, his foundation logo, and personal slogans. For an even more personal touch, the lettering is a scaled version of Andy's own handwriting. When designing the mural considerations had to be made for the placement of the athletic and entertainment equipment.

pages.title: Austin Postcard Mural
pages.narrative: This mural, painted 10 feet tall and 20 feet wide on the side of Roadhouse Relics , has garnered a considerable amount of attention. Countless Christmas cards (bottom photo), band photos and local magazines have used this as a backdrop. It can also can be seen on the back cover of a coffee table book about Austin, and in a Russell Crowe video. This kind of attention is great for business.

pages.title: Aztec Mural for Casino El Camino
pages.narrative: This mural created to finalize the look of the Casino El Camino patio had many challenges. "Casino", the owner, wanted to open up his enclosed patio with "windows" that look out onto an Aztec landscape. The red stucco wall, that matched the tile, already had the skull light sconces in place which we created years earlier. Furthermore, the texture of the wall was such, that we couldn't just paint the scene convincingly on the wall. Therefore, it was decided we would cut into the wall to create openings for the mural to fit into, creating the illusion of architecture in front of a landscape. The landscape imagery, inspired by 19th century explorer and artist Frederick Catherwood , was painted on wooden panels at the shop using outdoor quality sign paint. During this process, we also had our team cutting into the wall, framing out the openings, and finally match the existing stucco. The wall itself was then painted to resemble an ancient stone wall, matching the rest of the walls in the patio.

pages.title: Blue Ribbon Day Mural

warnings: no authored alt text for any image

pages.title: Camp Bow Wow
pages.narrative: This 8' x 8' mural was created for Camp Bow Wow, a new kennel in Round Rock, TX. The owners of this business wanted dogs playing in a camp area with a view of Austin, TX in the background. For fun, we added portraits of their own dogs at either side of the mural. To keep the cost down, this mural was painted on two 4' x 8' panels in our shop, and then installed at the kennel. Also, when murals are painted on panels, they can easily be relocated if the business moves to another location.

The idea of using a classic painting seemed like a good choice. Based on several different Cezanne still lifes, this 50 foot by 10 foot mural is actually a bas-relief sculpture made up of 26 pieces.

pages.title: Duluth Theater Mural
pages.description: This 20' x 31' mural was done for a new theatre in Duluth, Minnesota.
pages.narrative: This 20' x 31' mural was done for a new theatre in Duluth, Minnesota. After the design was approved, we painted the mural on panels and shipped it to them. It was then installed by their contractors. The photos show individual panels from the mural, the entire composition, and a process shot in the studio.

pages.title: Facebook
pages.narrative: Facebook approached us in 2015 to create a new 64' long mural for a new floor they added to their office. Located in downtown Austin, TX this mural was painted off site and installed in one evening. This allowed the office to work without interruption while the mural was being produced, and get a fun surprise the morning after installation. Metaphorically, this mural explores the ups and downs of the creative process, and some of Facebook's key phrases. Photos by Gino Barasa

pages.title: Pulte Homes Murals
pages.narrative: Pulte Homes called us to redo their conference room in their local Austin headquarters. They wanted to add excitement and corporate identity to their decor without making it look "like a carnival". After a lengthy design process they decided on this look. The flag mural was designed to have employee award plaques added over time under the different categories. The 6' tall by 9' long Austin Postcard mural has photos of employees enjoying recreational activities mounted to the surface. These were designed to be easily replaced with new images over time. pages.title: RGM Advisors Mural
pages.narrative: Gensler, an architecture firm, was remodeling two stories of the Chase building in downtown Austin for their client, RGM Advisors (an investment bank). They had seen our "Good Morning Austin" mural" on 5th street, and came to us to design a mural which would be placed in the lounge dining area of the building. They knew they wanted robots, so we came up with this design. We decided to paint the mural on Sintra Board which would then be attached to the wall, allowing us to work at the shop (and out of the way of our clients), and also save on cost and time. The mural covers one wall, and two parts of a wall that hangs from the ceiling. The top image is a picture of the original design. The other two photos show the completed mural installed in the building.
